disease_label_per_paper: Enterococcus casseliflavus bacteremia with hemodialysis catheter-associated septic thrombophlebitis
presentation_summary: 72-year-old man with chronic renal failure on thrice-weekly hemodialysis through a permanent right internal jugular venous catheter was referred for prolonged fever and persistent enterococcal bacteremia.
He had chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, coronary artery disease, hypertension, and chronic methylprednisolone exposure after lung decortication.

Fever to 39 C recurred around hemodialysis sessions with chills; admission labs showed leukocytosis with neutrophil predominance, CRP 61 mg/L, procalcitonin 2.7 ng/mL, creatinine 3.8 mg/dL, and anemia.
Hospital blood cultures later identified Enterococcus casseliflavus; CT showed thrombus near the distal catheter tip and pulmonary embolus.
